title: Allow configuration of missing value placeholder in `st.dataframe`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In st.data_editor, when you dont have a value for a determined cell, it will be showed as None:
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/57851959/4e6ca678-8c7b-4ef1-aaef-780c49b210c2)


### Why?

Since it is very user-unfriendly (a non-tech person may not understand what means None), it will be interesting have a parameter in st.data_editor that allows to replace these None by, for example, empty string (""), that will looks like this, but only for view purposes, without messing up the output.
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/57851959/ca9674dd-046c-49dd-805c-d39c11cd7801)


### How?

a parameter like:
`
none_alias=""
`
that allows me to change the None showing in the table.

### Additional Context

_No response_

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: We decided against using an empty string as the default placeholder since it wouldn't be completely accurate. For example, there is a semantic difference between an empty string value and a `None` value in a text column, which couldn't be reflected with an empty string placeholder. However, for many use cases, this might not really matter. And making this configurable seems to be a pretty good solution for this 👍 Maybe calling it just `placeholder` could also be a good choice since it's a bit comparable to the empty state placeholders we recently added to some of our widgets.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: I like current `None` display - allows to distinguish between `None` and `""` empty string. If I want that removed - that's cheap and easy with `df_filled = df.fillna("")` or whatever (depends on what you want to see). Maybe for localization it would be nice to have a placeholder text value, like for other components.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Doing `df_filled = df.fillna("")` is a bit problematic since it changes the underlying types in the dataframe and therefore also impacts the user experience negatively. Unfortunately, I think there isn't any good workaround for this that doesn't have some downsides.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
hmm, looking at pandas `.format` - there's an `na_rep` property, which could be used exactly for this, if supported on Streamlit side (currently I saw no difference in my tests).

Example from docs: 

``` python
df = pd.DataFrame([[np.nan, 1.0, 'A'], [2.0, np.nan, 3.0]])
df.style.format(na_rep='MISS', precision=3)
```

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
I support this request. I would like to change only the visual representation of None values in my `st.dataframe` without altering the actual dataframe itself.

Example usecase:
I have both automatic and manual entries in my dataframe. Automatic requests have a PID from another system, while manual uploads do not include a PID. Although setting the PID to None is acceptable from a dataframe perspective, non-technical users may find this confusing. Instead, I would prefer to insert the string "manual" for those rows, while not altering the underlying dataframe.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: Excellent suggestion! Im workin on a Streamlit page as we speak where the DataFrame is an important part, and its really frustrating for me to be forced to have ”None” in LinkColumns. Cause thats the only value which will be rendered as plain text. You should be able to have any value you choose. Plz fix this asap team! 💜

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: There is situation when sorting order is important for a column and you can't switch on using text column instead of number column because sorted numbers are [10, 9, 8, ..., 1, 0] and sorted strings are ["9", "8", ... "2", "10",  "1", "0"]. So solution with filling na by empty string doesn't work. Please implement configuration of missing value placeholder.
